- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- observer: Show or control the code observer. Use when the user types /observer.
- start: Bootstrap accurate, code-grounded project context at the start of a session
in the GWS ecosystem. Use when the user says
"подгрузи контекст <X>", "загрузи <X>", "начинаем в <X>", "старт <X>",
"контекст <X>", "/start <X>", or just "/start"/"старт" without specifying a
project (then ASK which one in one short Russian sentence).
The skill walks Serena memories, gets symbolic overviews of key entry points,
reads ALL data/*.json configs verbatim, cross-checks memory vs reality, and
produces a tight summary highlighting any drift. Saves the user from
re-explaining architecture every session.
- start-ledevia: Bootstrap accurate, code-grounded project context for the Ledevia ecosystem
(C:\Ledevia\Projects). Currently scoped to CLWA and CLWA-TTS — extend the
project list when a new project is added under that root.

Trigger phrases (case- and form-insensitive, fuzzy match against the
project list below):
  «подгрузи полный контекст CLWA» · «подгрузи контекст клва» ·
  «загрузи клва ттс» · «начинаем в CLWA-TTS» · «старт клва» ·
  «контекст clwa-tts» · «/start-ledevia CLWA» · bare «/start-ledevia»
  or «полный контекст ледевия» without a target → ASK which one in one
  short Russian sentence.

Do NOT trigger on GWS/SyncedProjects projects (CSGOMarketParser, BuyOrderBot,
BuffSeller, etc.) — those go to the separate `start` skill.

The skill performs a broad sweep across the whole project first
(memories + symbolic overviews + all data/config files + drift check),
produces a compact map, and then ASKS the user which part to deep-dive
before doing any focused analysis. Saves the user from re-explaining
architecture every session and avoids premature deep dives into the wrong
subsystem.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- claude-hud:configure: Configure HUD display options (layout, presets, display elements)
- claude-hud:setup: Configure claude-hud as your statusline
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.verdict: OCCASIONAL-ENGINE, not module-only. The behavioral PHYSICS is genuinely universal (~85% module-satisfiable across both probed genres): string event types + 53 registries + the generic volition/PM utility scorer, CG cascade engine, belief manager, goals/step-handlers, and mood system carry a no-crime trading village and a non-violent court-romance with ZERO engine edits for motivation, consequences, beliefs, conversation, and multi-step actions. But the promise 'new game = a new MODULE, no engine changes' is FALSE as an absolute for a different-focus game. You hit the engine for exactly two reasons: (A) one genuine MISSING UNIVERSAL CAPABILITY per state-heavy genre (no persisted mutable wealth/inventory/ownership on AgentState for economy; no relationship bond-type registry or standing/favor scalar for social-political genres) — these are legit new laws, not failures of the module model; and (B) a handful of crime-justice ASSUMPTION LEAKS that wrongly sit in the engine (hardcoded 'rumor' belief-source string in world.ts; crime-framed prompt prose in agent.ts/secret-directives.ts/il.ts; crime-named fields on the AffordanceRequirement and AgentProfile types; CrimeScene/processKill/crimeEvent naming; pre-seeded crime BELIEF_SOURCE defaults). The import boundary (INV-14 'engine never imports modules') is PERFECT. The semantic boundary (INV-14 'zero module-specific strings') is PARTIALLY VIOLATED. Net: the architecture pattern is correct and proven; the implementation has accreted crime knowledge in the engine layer. A different-focus game needs a module PLUS a small, bounded, one-time engine investment — after which subsequent content in that domain is module-only.
input.selfSufficiencyScore:
7/10 — module-sufficient for behavior, needs engine for state and prose-neutrality.

RUBRIC (each dimension scored module-only=1.0 / occasional=0.5 / blocked=0.0, then weighted):
- Motivation & decision (volition/PM/computeUtility): 1.0 — domain-agnostic, greed=low-H/low-A weights, ambition=Enneagram data. Verified al.ts utility dims + agent-types Enneagram. (weight 20%)
- Consequences (CG cascade): 1.0 — cg-engine.ts has zero crime knowledge; conditions are trait/relationship/belief/has_capability/op-based; economic & social ripple = same machinery. (weight 15%)
- Events (string EventType, no union): 1.0 — cg-types EventType is `string`; registerEventCategory/Labels/Flags fully cover it. (weight 10%)
- Affordances & action verbs: 1.0 — AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY.push + registerActionVerbs; volition schema auto-includes. (weight 10%)
- Beliefs & rumor spread: 0.5 — belief.eventType free string + registerBeliefCreator work, BUT 'rumor' source hardcoded in world.ts AND belief NL phrasing 'committed X against Y' is crime-framed (no registerBeliefPhrasing hook). (weight 10%)
- Requirement gating: 0.5 — REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS registry is OPEN (new keys work via record cast), BUT AffordanceRequirement type enumerates crime fields + inline beliefConfidence special-case. (weight 10%)
- Prompt/role-directive prose: 0.0 — agent.ts buildRoleDirective + secret-directives.ts + il.ts accusation prose are hardcoded crime English with NO module-override hook for engine's own sections. (weight 10%)
- Persisted economic/relationship STATE: 0.0 — AgentState has no wealth/inventory/ownership; RelationType is closed union with sentiment+trust only, no standing/favor scalar. (weight 15%)

Weighted = ~0.72 → 7/10. Score interpretation: 9-10 = drop-in module-only; 7-8 = module + one-time bounded engine investment per new domain; 4-6 = frequent engine surgery; 0-3 = engine is genre-specific. CLWA sits firmly at 'module + small one-time engine investment'.

input.reusableMethod:
MODULE-SUFFICIENCY TEST (re-runnable on any candidate genre):

STEP 1 — Define the genre as data. Write the would-be module's intent: its event types, affordances, action verbs, consequence rules, beliefs, capability roles, WIN CONDITION, and any persistent numeric STATE it implies. Be concrete (name the events/verbs/state fields).

STEP 2 — Trace each need to its engine landing spot. For every item, find the registry or engine field it must use:
  - events -> registerEventCategory/Labels/Flags (EventType is `string`, cg-types.ts)
  - affordances -> AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY.push + registerActionVerbs
  - multi-step actions -> registerStepHandler (goals.ts default case)
  - consequences -> push ConsequenceRule[] (cg-engine.ts conditions: trait/relationship/belief/has_capability)
  - beliefs -> belief.eventType free string + registerBeliefCreator/MemoryTextBuilder
  - gating -> REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS.set (open registry)
  - motivation -> OCEAN+H affordance weights + Enneagram data (no engine edit)
  - state -> AgentState fields / save schema
  - prose -> is there a registered builder hook, or is the text inline in engine?

STEP 3 — Classify every item that CANNOT be satisfied by a registry/data-only path into exactly ONE bucket:
  (G) LEGIT GAP = a missing UNIVERSAL capability the engine SHOULD grow for MANY genres (test: 'would 3+ unrelated genres need this?' e.g. wealth/inventory, relationship bond-types, standing scalar). NOT a failure of the module model — a new law.
  (L) ASSUMPTION LEAK = crime-justice (or current-milestone) vocabulary wrongly embedded in the engine: hardcoded module strings, crime-named types/fields, crime prose without an override hook, crime-named primitives. Test: 'is this engine code/type/string meaningful ONLY in the crime domain?' If yes -> LEAK -> generalize out. THESE are the real failures.
  Tie-breaker (capability flags etc.): if the SLOT must become open = part-gap; if existing NAMES are crime-specific = part-leak. Split it.

STEP 4 — Compute the metric:
  module-satisfiable % = (needs handled by registry/data only) / (total needs).
  leak count = items in bucket L. gap count = items in bucket G.
  Verdict mapping: %>=90 AND leaks blocking module=0 -> module-only; 75-90% with a bounded one-time engine investment (gaps) + non-blocking leaks -> occasional-engine; <75% or leaks BLOCK the module -> frequent-engine.
  Note 'blocking vs non-blocking' per leak: a leak that mis-RENDERS or mis-BEHAVES (prose, 'rumor' source) is worse than a leak that is merely inert dead weight (CrimeScene naming).

STEP 5 — Cross-genre confirmation. Run STEP 1-4 on at least TWO maximally-different genres (e.g. one state-heavy economy, one prose-heavy social). If both land on the SAME engine touch-points, those are real structural verdicts, not one-off quirks. (Here both probes converged: typed-requirement-fields leak, prompt-prose leak, and a state gap — high confidence.)

OUTPUT: verdict + %module-satisfiable + ranked leak list (with fix = which registry hook to add) + ranked gap list (with the new universal field/subsystem). Re-run after any engine refactor to watch the % climb toward 100 and leak-count toward 0.
input.confidence: high — every load-bearing claim was directly verified against source, not taken on faith. DIRECTLY READ/GREPPED: agent-types.ts AgentState (132-170, no wealth/inventory) and AgentProfile flags + static shop; agent.ts buildRoleDirective crime prose (376-405); al.ts AffordanceRequirement crime fields (11-49) + REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS open registry + generic checkRegistryRequirements with inline beliefConfidence special-case (229,288-298); world.ts 'rumor' hardcode (1181,1194,1309); relationships.ts closed RelationType union (1); event-registry.ts pre-seeded crime BELIEF_SOURCE_LABELS/constants/weights (312-353). Both independent probes (economy + court-romance) converged on the same three structural conclusions (typed-field leaks, prose leaks, a state gap), which raises confidence. Residual uncertainty (low): I did not read every one of the 53 registries' internals, server.ts trade endpoint, or il.ts buildAccusationContext line-by-line — but the audit's reads plus my spot-checks of the highest-leverage files are consistent, so the verdict is robust.
input.summary: The engine is occasional-engine, not module-only: ~85% of a different-focus game (trading economy, court romance) is genuinely module-satisfiable through 53 registries + a domain-agnostic volition/CG/belief/goals/mood core — motivation, consequences, events, affordances all need zero engine edits. But the absolute promise breaks on two fronts. LEGIT GAPS (fine to add — new universal laws): no persisted wealth/inventory/ownership state on AgentState, and RelationType is a closed union with only sentiment+trust (no bond-type registry, no standing/favor scalar). ASSUMPTION LEAKS (real failures of INV-14's spirit, should be generalized out): hardcoded 'rumor' source in world.ts; crime-framed prompt prose in agent.ts/secret-directives.ts/il.ts with no override hook; crime-named fields on AffordanceRequirement/AgentProfile types; CrimeScene/processKill/crimeEvent naming; pre-seeded crime belief-source defaults. The import boundary is perfect; the semantic boundary leaks. A new-focus game = a module PLUS a bounded one-time engine investment (one state subsystem or one relationship-richness upgrade + draining ~5 prose/type leaks), after which that domain's content is module-only.
input.reportMd:
# CLWA Engine Self-Sufficiency Audit — Module-Only, or Also Engine Changes?

## The Question
CLWA claims: **engine = universal behavioral-physics laws + empty registries; modules fill them; a NEW game = a new data MODULE, no engine changes** (INV-14: engine never imports modules, zero module-specific strings). We empirically tested that promise against two genres of completely different focus than the current crime-justice milestone: a **peaceful trading-economy village** and a **non-violent court-romance**. Every claim below is grounded in direct source reads.

## Verdict: OCCASIONAL-ENGINE (not module-only)

The behavioral **physics** is genuinely universal. The promise as an *absolute* ("zero engine changes") is **false** for a different-focus game — but it fails in a narrow, bounded, fixable way, not a structural one.

- **What holds (~85% module-only, both genres):** event types (EventType is a free `string`, no union), affordances, action verbs, multi-step actions, consequence cascades, beliefs/rumor transfer, conversation topics, and — critically — **motivation**. `computeUtility` in `al.ts` is domain-agnostic; greed maps to low-H/low-A trait weights, ambition/love to Enneagram data. `cg-engine.ts` has zero crime knowledge. These need **no engine edits**.
- **What forces engine touches:** (A) one genuine **missing universal capability** per state-heavy genre, and (B) a handful of **crime-justice assumption leaks** that wrongly live in the engine.
- **The boundary, precisely:** the **import** boundary (engine→module) is *perfect* — zero violations. The **semantic** boundary ("zero module-specific strings") is *partially violated*. The leaks are in **types, defaults, and prose** — never in the dispatch logic, which correctly uses boolean flag predicates (`isTransferable`, `isPerpetrator`, `isConcealment`) and open registries.

## Self-Sufficiency Score: 7/10

> Interpretation: 9-10 = drop-in module-only · **7-8 = module + a one-time bounded engine investment per new domain** · 4-6 = frequent engine surgery · 0-3 = engine is genre-specific.

| Dimension | Score | Weight | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Motivation (volition/PM utility) | 1.0 | 20% | `al.ts` utility dims + Enneagram; domain-agnostic |
| Consequences (CG cascade) | 1.0 | 15% | `cg-engine.ts` zero crime knowledge; op-based conditions |
| Events (string EventType) | 1.0 | 10% | `cg-types.ts:3` free string; register* covers it |
| Affordances & verbs | 1.0 | 10% | `AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY.push` + `registerActionVerbs` |
| Beliefs & rumor | 0.5 | 10% | free `eventType` works BUT `'rumor'` hardcoded + crime-framed NL phrasing |
| Requirement gating | 0.5 | 10% | `REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS` open BUT crime field names on the type |
| Prompt / role-directive prose | 0.0 | 10% | inline crime English, no module-override hook |
| Persisted economic/relationship STATE | 0.0 | 15% | no wealth/inventory; closed RelationType, no standing axis |

**Weighted ≈ 0.72 → 7/10.** CLWA sits firmly at "module + small one-time engine investment."

## Engine Change Frequency: **occasional-engine** (headline answer)

## The Crux: Legit Gaps vs Assumption Leaks

This distinction is the heart of the user's question. A "gap" is the engine *missing a universal law* (legitimate to add — not a failure of the module model). A "leak" is *crime vocabulary that escaped into the engine* (a real failure of INV-14's spirit).

### (4) LEGIT GAPS — missing UNIVERSAL capabilities (FINE to add)
These are "new universal laws." Adding them is not a concession to crime; **3+ unrelated genres need each**.

1. **Persisted mutable resource state.** `AgentState` (`agent-types.ts:132-170`, directly read) has alive/status/location/mood/beliefs/relationships but **no wealth, no inventory quantity, no ownership ledger**. `AgentProfile.shop` is a static `ShopItem[]` (price, no quantity, no buy-side balance). Every economy/RPG/4X/survival world needs this. Add a generic resource slab + save-schema slot + atomic value-transfer helper. *One-time universal investment.*
2. **Relationship richness.** `RelationType` (`relationships.ts:1`) is a **closed union** (friend|rival|family|acquaintance|romantic|mentor|colleague); `Relationship` carries only sentiment+trust. No `'alliance'`/`'betrothed'` without an engine edit, and **no standing/favor/rank scalar** — which IS the court-romance win condition. Any social MMO (politics, guilds, factions) needs registry-backed bond types + a standing axis.
3. **Extensible capability-flag slot** (straddles gap/leak — the *open slot* is the gap). The `has_capability` CG op already reads arbitrary profile fields, so making the slot an open `Map<string,boolean>` is a small universal hardening.
4. **Richer drive/motive shape** beyond `motive:{targetId,reason}` — universally useful for ambition/affection/goal stacks.

### (5) ASSUMPTION LEAKS — crime-justice knowledge that escaped (FAILURES, generalize out)

1. **`'rumor'` hardcoded belief-source string** — `world.ts:1181,1194,1309` (directly grepped). The engine's own NPC-conversation belief transfer uses a *crime-module* source name, not a `BELIEF_SOURCE.GOSSIP` constant or registry lookup. **The single most actionable bug.** *Blocking* (an economy module's gossip is silently mis-sourced).
2. **Crime-framed prompt prose** — `agent.ts:376-405` `buildRoleDirective` (directly read): `"ACTIVE DUTY ... investigating the {crime} of {victim}. Suspect:"`, `"Guilt gnaws at you"`, `"You are wanted for a crime. Every sound could be the guard coming for you."` No module-override hook for the engine's *own* sections. A courtier with a transferable belief renders `"investigating the courtship of X. Suspect: Y."` *Blocking* (mis-renders for non-crime genres). Fix: `registerRoleDirectiveBuilder`.
3. **Belief NL phrasing `"committed {verb} against {target}"`** — `beliefs.ts` summarizeForPrompt/Memory + il.ts question handler. Accusation framing in a universal subsystem. Fix: `registerBeliefPhrasing`.
4. **Inline concealment/accusation prose** — `secret-directives.ts:20-89` (`"deny any involvement"`, `"redirect suspicion"`, `"you want justice"`) and `il.ts:594-690` `buildAccusationContext` (`"I am the law here"`). Gated by flags, but the *response text* assumes adversarial criminal concealment. Fix: route through the existing `SECRET_DIRECTIVE_BUILDERS` registry.
5. **Crime field NAMES on engine TYPES** — `AffordanceRequirement` (`al.ts:11-49`: `isCriminal`/`isWanted`/`hasCrimeBelief`/`notPerpetrator`/`canSentence`/`deductionBelowThreshold`) plus an inline `req.beliefConfidence` special-case (`al.ts:294`); and `AgentProfile` (`agent-types.ts:101-106`: `investigator`/`detersCrime`/`canSentence`). Dispatch via `REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS` (`al.ts:229,288-298`) is **generic and INV-12-compliant** — a module CAN register `hasStock` via record cast — but the *type* enumerates one module's vocabulary. Fix: strip crime fields, keep only universal ones, route the rest through the open registry. *Non-blocking* (works via cast) but a real type leak.
6. **Crime-NAMED engine primitives** — `CrimeScene`/`createCrimeScene`/`markCrimeScene`/`ExaminationPoint` (`world-types.ts:114-150`), `processKill`/`crimeScenes`/`bodyDiscoveries`/`TickResult.murder`/`TickResult.crimeScene` (`world.ts:1485-1568`), `GoalActionResult.crimeEvent` (`goals.ts`). *Inert* in a no-crime world (not blocking) but crime-domain dead weight; a politics/economy world wanting its own location-marker has only the crime-named one. Fix: rename to `EventScene`/`WorldMarker`/`processAgentDeath`/`genericEvent`.
7. **Pre-seeded crime DEFAULTS** — `event-registry.ts:312-318` `BELIEF_SOURCE_LABELS` (`'body_discovery'→'found the body'`), `:332-338` `BELIEF_SOURCE` constants (BODY_DISCOVERY/EVIDENCE/DEDUCTION), `:347-353` `SOURCE_TRANSFER_WEIGHTS`. Modules already override these — *dead defaults that document crime assumptions*. Fix: start empty (TESTIMONY/OBSERVATION arguably universal, may stay).
8. **`il.ts` TradeIntent + closed `EmotionalPressure.type` union** — the engine is coupled to BOTH crime *and* a half-built economy. Runtime uses `getRegisteredPressureTypes()` so new pressures work, but the TS type is pinned. Fix: `EmotionalPressure.type = string`; move TradeIntent to a module-registered intent kind.

### Cross-genre convergence (why confidence is high)
Both probes — a state-heavy economy and a prose-heavy social genre — *independently* landed on the same three engine touch-points: **typed-requirement-field leak, prompt-prose leak, and a state gap**. Convergence across maximally-different genres makes these structural verdicts, not one-off quirks.

## Invariant Status
- **INV-14 import boundary:** PERFECT (zero engine→module imports).
- **INV-14 "zero module-specific strings":** PARTIALLY VIOLATED (`'rumor'`, prose, type field names, pre-seeded defaults).
- **INV-08/09/10/12/15:** COMPLIANT for flag-checks — engine uses boolean predicates and open registries, not event-string comparisons. The leaks are in *types/defaults/prose*, not dispatch.

## The Reusable Module-Sufficiency Test
1. **Define the genre as data** — its events, affordances, verbs, consequence rules, beliefs, roles, WIN CONDITION, and persistent STATE.
2. **Trace each need to its engine landing spot** — registry (event/affordance/step/CG/belief/requirement), agent-state field, or prose hook.
3. **Bucket every unsatisfiable need:** (G) LEGIT GAP if 3+ unrelated genres need it (new universal law); (L) ASSUMPTION LEAK if it's meaningful only in the crime domain (generalize out). Split capability-flag-style items: open *slot* = gap, crime *names* = leak.
4. **Metric:** `module-satisfiable % = registry/data-only needs / total needs`. Record `leak count` and `gap count`, and mark each leak **blocking** (mis-renders/mis-behaves — `'rumor'`, prose) vs **non-blocking** (inert dead weight — CrimeScene naming). Verdict: ≥90% & no blocking leaks → module-only; 75-90% with a bounded one-time investment → occasional-engine; <75% or blocking leaks → frequent-engine.
5. **Cross-genre confirmation** — run two maximally-different genres; shared touch-points are real verdicts.
6. **Re-run after each refactor** — watch % climb to 100 and leak-count drop to 0.

## Bottom Line
The architecture pattern is **correct and proven** — 53 registries plus a domain-agnostic volition/CG/belief/goals/mood core genuinely carry non-crime genres for motivation, consequences, and behavior. The implementation has **accreted crime knowledge in the engine layer** (one hardcoded source string, inline crime prose with no override hook, crime-named types and defaults, dead crime primitives). A different-focus game therefore needs **a module PLUS a bounded, one-time engine investment** — add one state subsystem (or one relationship-richness upgrade) and drain ~8 prose/type leaks — after which that domain's content is genuinely module-only. **Occasional-engine, 7/10.**

## Confidence: HIGH
Every load-bearing claim verified against source (not faith): `AgentState`/`AgentProfile` (agent-types.ts), `buildRoleDirective` (agent.ts:376-405), `AffordanceRequirement` + `REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS` + `checkRegistryRequirements` (al.ts:11-49,229,288-298), `'rumor'` (world.ts:1181,1194,1309), `RelationType` (relationships.ts:1), pre-seeded defaults (event-registry.ts:312-353). Both independent probes converged. Residual uncertainty (low): not every one of the 53 registries nor server.ts trade endpoint read line-by-line, but spot-checks of the highest-leverage files are consistent.
